verdict.rationale: Jitsu's docs state it is "100% open-source" and self-hostable, and a public GitHub repository (jitsucom/jitsu) exists. Its llms.txt calls it an open-source platform, and a community user reports using the open-source version. However, the evidence never names the license or its terms, so the "open license" part of the story is asserted rather than documented. missing for 10: the specific license name/terms (e.g., a LICENSE file citation), clarity on whether all components (including enterprise/cloud features) are covered by the open license.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Jitsu is 100% open-source and can be deployed to any on-premise infrastructure.
Jitsu is an open-source data integration platform and a self-hostable alternative to Segment.
We've started using the open source version for one of the tools we are building
